# Golden fixtures

Generated by `scripts/golden` (see its README for how to run it and which
upstream versions it pins). Do not edit by hand. Regenerate instead.

Each fixture `<name>` is a pair:

- `<name>.excalidraw`: the input, an ordinary `.excalidraw` file as
  excalidraw.com would save it. Every Element carries an explicit `seed`.
- `<name>.golden.json`: what Excalidraw draws for each Element of that file.

| Fixture        | Covers                                                                              |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shapes`       | rectangle, diamond, ellipse x roughness 0/1/2 x solid/dashed/dotted x sharp/round; tiny and narrow Elements (roughness reduction); medium and large ones (less jitter on long lines, fixed and custom corner radii) |
| `fills`        | hachure, cross-hatch, zigzag, solid on every closed shape at each roughness; rounded shapes; stroke widths; fills under dashed and dotted outlines; a large rough ellipse |
| `lines-arrows` | lines and arrows: straight, multi-point, curved (every roughness), closed (filled) loops; every arrowhead at start and end; dashed, dotted, thick; long ones; small ones (roughness reduction, which round lines escape) |
| `arrowhead-turns` | every arrowhead at the start and end of arrows whose last segment is short and turns away; thick and curved variants |
| `freedraw`     | simulated and real (stylus) pressure; thick, precise, dot, short, closed and filled strokes |
| `text`         | text Elements laid out by Excalidraw itself (see below): alignments, rotation, font families, fixed-width wrapping (hyphens, spaces, long words, CJK), labels in rectangles, ellipses and diamonds, and on arrows (straight, multi-point, curved; wrapped to the arrow's width) |

## `text.excalidraw`

Has no `.golden.json`: the file is its own golden. Excalidraw's `wrapText`,
`measureText` and `computeBoundTextPosition` laid every text out with a fake
measurer in which each character is half as wide as the font is high, and saved
the result: wrapped `text`, `originalText`, and the position and size of each
text and of its container. The core, given the same fake `TextMeasurer`, must
wrap `originalText` into the saved lines at the saved positions.

## `.golden.json`

```json
{
"format": 1,
"upstream": {"excalidraw": "<commit>", "roughjs": "4.6.4", "perfect-freehand": "1.2.0"},
"elements": {
  "<element id>": [ <shape>, <shape>, ... ]
}
}
```

`elements` has one entry per non-deleted Element of the `.excalidraw` file, keyed
by its `id`. Its value lists the Element's shapes in z-order (fill before
stroke, arrowheads after the line). Coordinates are in the Element's own frame:
the origin is the Element's `x`/`y` (rotation is not applied). Colours and
opacity are not part of the output; read them from the Element.

A shape is one of:

```json
{"kind": "rough", "shape": "rectangle", "options": {...}, "sets": [<set>, ...]}
{"kind": "outline", "points": [[x, y], ...]}
```

- `rough` is a rough.js `Drawable`. `shape` is rough.js' name for it
  (`rectangle`, `polygon`, `ellipse`, `path`, `curve`, `linearPath`, `line`,
  ...). `options` are the resolved rough.js options *as Excalidraw chose them*
  (e.g. adjusted roughness, `strokeLineDash`, `fillWeight`, `hachureGap`,
  `preserveVertices`); the renderer's stroke width, dash and fill weight come
  from here. rough.js' internal random generator is omitted.
- `outline` is the closed polygon perfect-freehand computes for a freedraw
  stroke (`getFreedrawOutlinePoints`), in order. Fill it to draw the stroke.

A `<set>` is a rough.js `OpSet`:

```json
{"type": "path", "ops": [{"op": "move", "data": [x, y]}, {"op": "bcurveTo", "data": [x1, y1, x2, y2, x, y]}, {"op": "lineTo", "data": [x, y]}]}
```

`type` is `path` (stroke the ops), `fillPath` (fill the ops as one shape) or
`fillSketch` (stroke the ops as hachure-like lines, with `options.fillWeight`).

Numbers are written by JavaScript's `JSON.stringify`, i.e. they are the exact
doubles upstream produced. Tests compare with a small tolerance anyway.

## Reading from Rust

`crates/drawing/src/test_support.rs` reads both files with the core's own JSON
(`pkm_base::json`) into `Shape`, `OpSet` and `Op` values:
`Fixture::load("shapes").shapes("rectangle-r0-solid-sharp")`.
The `golden` tests in `crates/drawing/src/rough.rs` check that the fixtures are complete.
